prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: The monocular depth map depicts a downward-angled egocentric view of an outdoor concrete ground plane (~1.5 to 2.0 metres below the camera wearer) with no other people present, where the wearer's own torso, forearms, and gloved hands appear brightest at the bottom edge (0.2 to 0.6 metres away) while holding the near end of a long wooden plank within arm's reach. The held plank extends away from the wearer from roughly 0.4 metres at the bottom center/left to over 2.5 metres toward the upper-right in frame 1 and upper-center in frames 2–5, suspended above blue metal sawhorse legs (~0.8 to 1.8 metres away on the left and bottom-right), shorter wooden boards lying flat on the concrete to the upper-left (~1.8 to 2.8 metres away), and a wheeled tool cart partly out of view at the right edge (~1.5 to 2.0 metres away, ~1.0 metre to the right of the plank). Across the 5 frames, the camera wearer turns and shifts leftward from frame 1 to frame 2 so the plank rotates from a diagonal orientation to point straight ahead, and in frame 5 the top plank shifts slightly rightward to reveal a second stacked plank directly underneath it. Compared to RGB alone, the depth map clearly separates the elevated plank and sawhorse crossbars from the underlying concrete surface and eliminates deceptive cast shadows on the ground. However, the depth map is unreliable in frame 1 where the concrete floor on the upper-left appears anomalously bright (nearer) than the right side, and across frames 2–5 where thin blue sawhorse legs and distant plank ends lose sharp depth boundaries and blend into the dark background.
descriptions.segmentation: The instance segmentation map detects only fragments of the scene against a black background, showing a pink 'person' mask at the bottom of frames 1, 2, 3, and 5 corresponding to the camera wearer's own lower torso, right forearm, or gloved left hand (0.2 to 0.6 metres away, facing downward/forward along the plank with no other people in the scene), alongside a large brown 'surfboard' mask in frame 1. In frame 1, the wearer's torso mask at the bottom center/left (0.2 to 0.5 metres away) partially occludes the near end of the wooden plank and the ground beneath, while the brown mask spans from roughly 0.4 to 2.5 metres across the middle of the frame. Across the 5 frames, the segmentation changes erratically as the camera wearer turns after frame 1: the large brown mask disappears completely in frames 2–5, and the 'person' mask shrinks to just the gloved left hand gripping the plank's left edge (~0.6 metres away, within arm's reach) in frame 2, switches to only the right forearm at the bottom-center (~0.3 metres away) in frame 3, drops out entirely in frame 4, and reappears on the right forearm and shirt sleeve in frame 5. While the 'person' mask in frames 1, 3, and 5 helps isolate the camera wearer's immediate body boundary at the lower edge of the field of view, it provides almost no spatial information that is hard to see in RGB alone. Overall, the map is highly unreliable because it misclassifies the wooden plank and large patches of the surrounding concrete floor and wheeled cart as a 'surfboard' in frame 1, completely misses the planks, sawhorses, and ground in frames 2–5, and fails to segment the wearer's visible hands and arms consistently across frames.
descriptions.pose: The body and hand skeleton map is completely blank (solid black) across all 5 frames, failing to detect any yellow body keypoints or magenta hand skeletons anywhere in the scene. In the RGB strip, no other people are present to face or look toward the camera wearer, as the viewpoint looks steeply downward at the concrete ground (~1.5 to 2.0 metres below) while the camera wearer faces forward along the wooden plank. Although the camera wearer's own gloved left hand (~0.5 to 0.7 metres away on the left edge of the plank) and right forearm and hand (~0.3 to 0.5 metres away at the bottom-center/right) are within arm's reach and actively holding the near end of the plank across all 5 frames as the wearer turns between frames 1 and 2, their head, shoulders, and lower body remain out of the field of view behind the camera. Because the map is entirely empty, it reveals nothing beyond the RGB image and is completely unreliable for tracking the egocentric wearer's visible forearms and gloved hands due to severe self-occlusion, steep top-down viewing angles, and truncation at the bottom frame boundary.
